title: Rollout gate dashboard template and trace oracles
content:
Purpose:
- Short-working draft for a canonical dashboard template used as a rollout gate (canary -> small %, canary pass/fail) tied directly to a small set of trace "oracles" (anchored traces used to validate hypotheses).
- Goal: give PMs/SEs a reproducible checklist and dashboard skeleton they can attach to every model or config rollout so rollout decisions are data-driven, cost-bounded, and fast to interpret.

Audience:
- Release engineers, SREs, product owners running canaries, solutions eng for customers doing dedicated rollouts.

Constraints / guiding principles:
- Keep query cost <= 1500 monthly queries per rollout by default (budgeted to team).
- O(1) visual surface: single row per SLI + one compact trace panel per hypothesis. Avoid >6 visible panels.
- Each rollout dashboard ties to a single experiment id and includes source model/version and traffic split.
- Alert gating must be simple: PASS/DEGRADED/FAIL with explicit next steps.

Metric contract (minimal required SLIs) - definitions and rationale:
1) user-visible latency p50/p90/p99 (ttft = time-to-first-token):
   - name: inference.ttft.ms
   - definition: time from API request ingress to first byte emitted to client (ms).
   - why: user perceived latency; more sensitive to prefix caching and routing fallbacks.

2) token tail latency p99 (server side):
   - name: runtime.token_emit.p99.ms
   - definition: wall clock interval between emission of last token and previous event for longest requests in a quantile window.
   - why: catches token-level stalls (KV miss thrash, kernel stalls).

3) model-quality regression indicator (approx): top-level pass-rate on golden prompts:
   - name: rollout.quality.pass_rate
   - definition: fraction of golden prompt set where top-ranked response score >= baseline_threshold over sample N=200.
   - why: cheap guard against obvious regressions. Not a full eval, but fast signal.

4) kv-cache warm-hit ratio (session-weighted):
   - name: kvcache.session_hit_ratio
   - definition: weighted hits/(hits+misses) where weight = session request count.
   - why: rollout can change prefix behavior (different tokenization/quantization) and dramatically affect cost & latency.

5) continuous-batch size median & 95th percentile:
   - name: batching.size.p50 and batching.size.p95
   - definition: per-second distribution of inferred batch sizes observed by serving nodes.
   - why: batching changes cost, and sudden drops imply degraded throughput or bad routing.

6) fallback rate (model-level):
   - name: routing.fallback_rate
   - definition: fraction of requests that were auto-routed to fallback model/region due to capacity/latency policy in the window.
   - why: indicates resilience but also masked regressions. High fallback on canary == FAIL unless expected.

Trace oracles: concept and recipes
- Concept: a tiny curated set of 6–12 traces per rollout mapped to specific hypotheses. Each trace is annotated with the hypothesis, expected metric ranges, and the anchor points (span names) to inspect.
- Example hypotheses + oracle traces:
  H1: KV eviction thrash on long chats -> trace oracle: multi-turn session with repeated prefix use; anchor spans: kvcache.lookup, kvcache.populate, runtime.kernel_queue_wait.
  H2: quantized-kernel stutter under long sequence -> trace oracle: single large-seq request; anchor spans: matmul.quant_exec, matmul.float_exec (compare durations).
  H3: routing-induced cold-start -> trace oracle: first request after node spin-up; anchor spans: node.init, model.load, kvprefetch.init.
- Storage: persistent trace id list stored under the experiment namespace (not endless); prefer sampling to keep cost low.

Sampling policy for oracles:
- Always capture full spans for any request that matches (experiment_id && golden_prompt_set) for the first 2k requests after rollout start. After that, sample 1/1000.
- Keep a pinned set of 12 recent oracles for quick replay and to attach to the dashboard.

Dashboard layout template (compact):
- Header: experiment id, model:version, start time, traffic split.
- Row A (SLIs summary): PASS|DEGRADED|FAIL big badge computed from thresholds below.
- Row B (Latency): ttft p50/p90/p99 sparkline + anomaly markers.
- Row C (Cost signals): batching size p50/p95, kvcache.session_hit_ratio sparkline, estimated per-request token cost.
- Row D (Quality): rollout.quality.pass_rate bar + example failing prompts (sampled).
- Row E (Fallback & routing): fallback_rate, region-fallback heatmap.
- Row F (Trace oracles): list of 6 pinned trace links with short annotations and direct open-in-trace-view buttons.

Pass criteria (starter):
- ttft p99 increased <= 10% vs baseline AND
- rollout.quality.pass_rate >= baseline - 1.5% absolute AND
- fallback_rate <= 2% absolute over baseline
- kvcache.session_hit_ratio drop <= 5% relative
If ANY of these violated -> mark DEGRADED. If two or more violated -> FAIL.
(These are starting heuristics; product/SE should set for each experiment.)

Alerting and automated gating
- Soft alerts: Slack + email to rollout owner when a single SLI exceeds soft threshold.
- Hard gates: automated rollback trigger if FAIL persists for >10 minutes with >5% traffic.
- Manual override: release engineer can override to continue with explicit reason and follow-up ticket. Record override in the dashboard panel.

Query budget and cost controls
- Default budget (per rollout): 1500 dashboard queries total/month, 200 pinned full-trace fetches.
- If golden prompt evaluation is enabled, run it offline in batch once per hour rather than live to save queries.
- Use condensed trace preview (first 200 spans only) by default; full-trace fetch counts toward the 200 per-month budget.

Operational runbook (short)
- Step 0: verify experiment meta (model, rollout id) on header.
- Step 1: sanity -> check SLI summary badge. If PASS -> continue.
- Step 2: if DEGRADED -> open pinned oracles for H1..H3. Check span timings and look for consistent skew across samples.
- Step 3: if FAIL -> open sequence of fallback events and traffic-split timeline. If fallback rate spiked, rollback.
- Step 4: file follow-up (linked artifact) with direct sample traces attached and set priority.

Ownership & responsibilities:
- Release owners tag the dashboard at rollout creation.
- Observability team provides the dashboard template and maintains the trace capture sampler.
- SREs triage first hour after rollout; product owner reviews quality signals within 24 hours.

Open questions / TODOs:
- (A) How strict should we be on pass thresholds for embedded customers? (privacy & sampling implications)
- (B) Can we get a cheaper approximate token-cost estimator to show on the dashboard instead of running the token counter query for every window?
- (C) Confirm retention policy for pinned oracle traces (30 days vs 90 days).
- (D) Add a small synthetic probe that mimics a 15-turn chat at T-1 cadence to measure KV warmth proactively — needs infra work.

Quick links & references:
- related: ENGOBS-1023 (rollout gating spec draft)
- telemetry PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/317
- slack: #observability (thread linked above)

Notes to self:
- keep the dashboard narrow; product people prefer one-glance PASS/FAIL.
- show example failing golden prompt responses inline (preview) to make quality regressions obvious.
- when prototyping, start with 3 golden prompts, not 200, to keep cost down - expand if noisy.

End of draft.
